question: On Linux, with no Windows machine in the loop, what does each Python call path of the owalnuts package cost per gradient relative to a pure-Rust target on the WP47 models, and does the nutpie per-gradient gap on those PyMC models (WP47, WP58, measured on Windows) persist?

predecessors.WP58: STUDIES/nutpie_per_gradient_gap_v1 (Windows, contended; the gap on the same three PyMC models)

seed_check: exact-word git grep over main and every local wt/* branch, and grep -rw over ~/lanes on the box, found none of 7878101-7878103 or 7878501 (recorded in PREREGISTRATION.md)
model_source: callpath_targets.py copied verbatim from STUDIES/python_callpath_v1 (identical in nutpie_per_gradient_gap_v1); models/hier_data.json copied verbatim from nutpie_per_gradient_gap_v1/models; the Rust arm's densities are WP58's native ones

arm_definitions.rust: pure-Rust reference: rust/ harness (wp78-rust), native densities, owalnuts::sampler::Sampler at its defaults configured as the Python package configures it, starts Init::default() (best-of-16) via candidate_starts; release profile = the extension's (opt 3, lto, codegen-units 1)
arm_definitions.cfunc: owalnuts.from_cfunc of the documented recipe: numba cfunc with error_model='numpy' and the nonfinite guard around the njit kernel (WP47 'cfunc-safe', callpath_targets.cfunc_safe_target)
arm_definitions.py-njit: plain Python callable around the same njit kernel (transport control; WP47 showed it bit-identical to cfunc-safe)
arm_definitions.pymc-gilfree: owalnuts.from_pymc(model, gil_free=True) (PyTensor NUMBA jit_fn in a numba cfunc)
arm_definitions.pymc: owalnuts.from_pymc(model): PyTensor C backend, a Python callable; thread_safe=False at threads=1, thread_safe=True at threads=4 (the documented rule)
arm_definitions.jax: owalnuts.from_jax(logp) (jit=True default; the post-WP47 numpy-argument dispatch)
arm_definitions.nutpie: nutpie 0.16.8: nutpie.compile_pymc_model(model) (numba backend), nutpie.sample(draws=1000, tune=1000, chains=4, cores=threads, seed, save_warmup=True), defaults otherwise

threads_note: owalnuts threads / nutpie cores; 4 chains in every cell; every process pinned to cores 12-15

sampler.settings: owalnuts.sample at the package defaults (init=None = best-of-16); nutpie defaults

order: strictly sequential child processes; micro cells first (targets outer, micro_paths rotated by target index); then seeds outer, targets, the (arm x threads) list over owalnuts_arms + nutpie_arms rotated by (3 * seed index + target index)

metrics.wall_per_gradient_us: Rust-side sampling wall (SampleResult.wall_seconds; the harness's Sampler::run wall) / kernel target calls; at threads=4 this is throughput per gradient across the 4 chains. Python-arm walls exclude start selection; the Rust arm's run wall excludes it too
metrics.latency_vs_rust: median over seeds of wall_per_gradient_us(path) / the same for rust at the same thread count; and the difference in us at threads=1
metrics.micro: median of 10^4 individually timed calls through the Python surface (cfunc and pymc-gilfree through ctypes, labelled); rust: median of 10^4 Instant-timed native evaluations and a 10^4-call loop mean
metrics.functionals: every unconstrained coordinate plus theta_1..theta_8 for eight (callpath_targets.functionals)
metrics.ess_per_second: min bulk ESS / wall of the owalnuts.sample or nutpie.sample call (rust: start selection + Sampler::run); compilation excluded and reported as construct_seconds
metrics.ess_per_gradient: min bulk ESS / total gradients: oWALNUTS kernel target calls + best-of-16 start-selection evaluations (Python arms: counted after the run from owalnuts.best_of_starts(return_details=True), untimed; rust: counted); nutpie: n_steps warmup + draws
metrics.nutpie_gap: per model: geomean over seeds of nutpie ESS/gradient (cores=1 cells) / geomean over seeds of the arm's ESS/gradient (threads=1 cells); primary arm pymc (the WP58 Python path); pooled = geomean over the three models
metrics.ratio_aggregation: ESS/s ratios are geometric means over seeds of per-seed ratios (same seed, matched threads/cores)
metrics.bit_identity: sha256 of the (chains, draws, dim) retained float64 draws

P1.text: in-sampler wall per gradient at threads=1 (us, every seed's median) lies in these ranges

P2.text: cost relative to the pure-Rust target (median wall per gradient ratio, same threads)

P3.text: threads=4 vs threads=1 (geomean over seeds of per-seed ESS/s ratios)

P4.text: bit identity: rust == cfunc == py-njit on every model, seed and thread count; every oWALNUTS arm identical at threads 1 and 4; nutpie identical at cores 1 and 4; pymc != pymc-gilfree on eight and hier (C vs NUMBA backend, WP47); the Python arms' best-of-16 chosen candidates and evaluation counts equal the Rust arm's

P5.text: ESS per gradient of every oWALNUTS arm within 0.8-1.25x of rust (geomean over seeds, threads=1 cells), every model

P6.text: the nutpie per-gradient gap persists on Linux

P7.text: ESS/s vs nutpie at matched threads/cores (geomean over seeds of per-seed ratios), every model

P8.text: health and completion: every one of the 126 sampler cells and 18 micro cells completes with status ok and exit code 0 (including pymc thread_safe=True at threads=4: F6 on Linux / CPython 3.12, untested by WP47); every oWALNUTS arm passes the gates on >= 8 of its 9 (model, seed) cells at threads=1; nutpie fails the gates on eight in >= 2 of 3 seeds and passes gauss100 3/3 and hier >= 2/3

decision_rule.R1: PyMC first choice. If pymc-gilfree at threads=4 has ESS/s >= 2.0x pymc at threads=1 (geomean over seeds of per-seed ratios) on every model, completes every cell, and passes at least as many gate cells as pymc threads=1 on each model, the README recommends from_pymc(model, gil_free=True) with threads=4 as the first choice for PyMC models on Linux. Otherwise from_pymc(model) at threads=1 stays first and gil_free is listed as an opt-in with its measured ratio.
decision_rule.R2: PyMC vs nutpie, per model class (gauss100 = well-scaled smooth, eight = small funnel-shaped hierarchical, hier = larger hierarchical regression). If nutpie cores=4 ESS/s >= 1.25x the R1 path's ESS/s (geomean over seeds) and nutpie passes the gates on >= 2/3 seeds of that model, the README says nutpie is faster on that class by the measured ratio. If nutpie fails the gates on >= 2/3 seeds of a model, the README states the gate failure instead of a speed comparison. Otherwise the README says oWALNUTS's R1 path is at least competitive (ratio stated).
decision_rule.R3: Hand-written kernels. If cfunc threads=4 ESS/s >= 2.0x py-njit threads=1 ESS/s on every model, the README recommends from_cfunc (error_model='numpy' + guard) for speed. If cfunc's wall per gradient at threads=4 is <= 1.5x rust's on every model, the README says from_cfunc runs within 1.5x of a native Rust target; otherwise it states the measured ratio.
decision_rule.R4: Threads for Python callables. For each of py-njit, jax and pymc: if its threads=4 / threads=1 ESS/s ratio is < 1.0 on >= 2 of 3 models, the README keeps 'use threads=1' for that path on Linux; if it is >= 1.2 on every model, the README says threads=4 helps that path on Linux; otherwise it says threads makes little difference.
decision_rule.R5: The nutpie per-gradient sentence. If the pooled pymc gap is in [1.4, 2.1] and every model's gap is > 1.2: 'persists on Linux' with the Linux numbers. If the pooled gap is < 1.25: the README says it did not reproduce on Linux. Otherwise: 'smaller on Linux' with the numbers.
decision_rule.R6: JAX. If jax threads=1 ESS/s >= 0.5x py-njit threads=1 ESS/s on every model, the README says from_jax is competitive with a compiled callable; otherwise it states that JAX's per-call dispatch dominates small models, with the measured us per gradient.
decision_rule.scope: The rule decides documentation only. No library code or default is changed by this study; failures are results and are not rerun.

smoke.note: after the freeze, before the first evidence cell: plumbing only, seed 1, WP78_ART outside artifacts/, outputs deleted; not evidence

environment.box: AWS EC2 c7a.4xlarge, 16 dedicated AMD EPYC cores (no SMT), 32 GB, Ubuntu 24.04; lane 4 = cores 12-15; three other lanes active (shared L3 and memory bandwidth): walls are pinned, co-tenanted
environment.packages_requested: numpy 2.4.6, numba 0.67.0, jax[cpu] 0.10.2, pymc 5.28.5, pytensor 2.38.2, nutpie 0.16.8, arviz 0.23.4, maturin 1.15.0 (WP47's versions); exact freeze in artifacts/build-manifest.json
environment.extension: maturin develop --release in integrations/python of this branch's clone on the box, Rust 1.88.0, taskset -c 12-15, 4 build jobs
environment.env: RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, PYTENSOR_FLAGS=compiledir=<lane cache>, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR=<lane cache>
